title: Encapsulation Packet Protocol
issue: Recommended Standard, Issue 3 (Blue Book), with Editorial Change 1 (November 2020)
organisation: Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS)
status_notes: The Document Control table (PDF p. 7) lists 133.1-B-1 'Encapsulation Service' (June 2006) and 133.1-B-2 (October 2009) as superseded and 133.1-B-3 (May 2020) as the 'Current issue'. Issue 3 removes the Space Packet from the available encapsulation formats, renames 'Encapsulation Service' to 'Encapsulation Packet Protocol' and adds USLP to the supported data link protocols. EC 1 (November 2020) updates obsolete text in the page header.
summary:
The CCSDS Recommended Standard for the **Encapsulation Packet Protocol (EPP)**. EPP is a thin 'shim' protocol that lets the [TM](../ccsds/tm-sdlp.md), [TC](../ccsds/tc-sdlp.md), [AOS](../ccsds/aos.md), Proximity-1 and [USLP](../ccsds/uslp.md) data link protocols carry data units that have no CCSDS-authorised Packet Version Number. Examples are IP datagrams (through IP over CCSDS), DTN/LTP traffic and private mission data. Each user data unit goes unchanged into one Encapsulation Packet (Packet Version Number '111', 'Version 8 CCSDS Packet'), which then travels in a VC, MAP or Proximity-1 packet service. Earlier issues (called 'Encapsulation Service') could also wrap data in a [Space Packet](../ccsds/space-packet.md); issue 3 removes that option.

Section 2 gives the concept and features: one-way, asynchronous, unconfirmed and order-preserving delivery with possible gaps. Users are addressed by the Encapsulation Protocol Identifier (EPI), and a SAP combines PVN, EPI and the SDLP channel (GVCID, GMAP ID and so on). Section 3 defines the ENCAPSULATION.request and ENCAPSULATION.indication primitives.

Section 4 specifies the packet. The variable header is 1, 2, 4 or 8 octets: version, 3-bit EPI, 2-bit Length of Length, then (for the longer headers) a 4-bit User Defined field, a 4-bit EPI Extension, a 2-octet CCSDS Defined field and a 1, 2 or 4-octet Packet Length that counts the whole packet. Table 4-2 gives the resulting size limits, from a 1-octet idle packet to 4,294,967,295 octets. The section also covers Encapsulation Idle Packets (EPI '000'), the extended-ID escape ('110') and private data ('111'). Section 5 lists the managed parameters, and the annexes note that EPP has no security of its own ([SDLS](../ccsds/sdls.md) or BPSec provide it) and rename the two SANA protocol-ID registries.

key_points.text: Issue 3 removes the Space Packet as an encapsulation format, renames the standard from 'Encapsulation Service' to 'Encapsulation Packet Protocol' and adds USLP support.
EPP carries CCSDS-recognised protocol data units that lack an authorised Packet Version Number over the packet services of the Space Data Link Protocols.
One user data unit goes unchanged into one Encapsulation Packet; delivery is one-way and unconfirmed, preserves order, and may have gaps.
A SAP is identified by PVN + EPI + SDLP channel; the channel is the GVCID for VCP services and the GMAP ID for TC and USLP MAP Packet services.
An Encapsulation Packet is 1 to 4,294,967,295 octets: a 1 to 8-octet header plus 0 to 4,294,967,287 octets of encapsulated data.

Header fields: Packet Version Number (3 bits, '111'), EPI (3 bits), Length of Length (2 bits), then optionally User Defined (4 bits), EPI Extension (4 bits), CCSDS Defined (2 octets) and Packet Length (1, 2 or 4 octets).

EPI '000' marks an Encapsulation Idle Packet (usable as the idle packet of TM, AOS and USLP), '110' means the EPI Extension field identifies the protocol, and '111' means mission-specific private data.
Length of Length '00', '01', '10', '11' gives a Packet Length field of 0, 1, 2 or 4 octets; '00' is allowed only for a one-octet idle packet.
The Packet Length field holds the total packet length in octets, header included (unlike the Space Packet's length-minus-one).
Maximum packet sizes for 2, 4 and 8-octet headers are 255, 65,535 and 4,294,967,295 octets (Table 4-2); the 4-octet length accommodates IPv6 jumbograms.
Managed parameters: minimum and maximum data unit length, and the valid (and valid extended) Encapsulation Protocol Identifiers from SANA.
EPP provides no security; SDLS (355.0-B, 355.1-B) at the data link layer or the Bundle Security Protocol at the network layer can be used.

notes: The slug's 'e1' is Editorial Change 1 (November 2020); the Document Control page footer carries an extra 'November 2020' date. PDF pages 1 and 2 are duplicate cover pages. The extraction has 34 PDF pages (registry: 33); the last page is blank. Section 2.2 repeats one sentence about timing relationships and data generation rate almost verbatim. Annex A2.1 speaks of 'two modified SANA registry requests', and A2.2 lists no new registries. Normative references [1] to [5] still cite the 2015 issues of TM, TC and AOS and USLP issue 1 (2018). Section 1.7 references 'constitute provisions of this document' (kind 'normative'); Annex C lists informative references. No individual authors are named.
